title: Having met the unageing, who would delight in long life?
theme: A mortal who has come near the undying, and knows the difference, will not cling to the pleasures of beauty and love, nor rejoice in a very long life.

words.meaning: of those who do not age

words.context: Śaṅkara: «कुः पृथिवी अधश्चासावन्तरिक्षादिलोकापेक्षया तस्यां तिष्ठतीति क्वधःस्थः»

sandhi.rule: Final m before a vowel is kept: ajīryatām amṛtānām upetya.
n before m is kept; written together.
kaḥ before r becomes ko, P. 6.1.114 (हशि च) and P. 6.1.87 (आद्गुणः).

samasa.meaning: standing on the earth, which is below; the vigraha is Śaṅkara’s

samasa.vigraha: वर्णान् च रतीः च प्रमोदान् च

morphology.note: Absolutive of upa-i, ‘having approached’; with the genitive amṛtānām (‘to the presence of the immortals’, Śaṅkara: «सकाशम् उपेत्य»).
Optative middle of ram, in a rhetorical question: ‘who would delight?’ — no one.

translation.literal: Having approached the unageing immortals, [what] ageing mortal standing on the earth below, knowing, reflecting on [the passing nature of] beauty, love and delights, would delight in a very long life?
translation.readable: Who, having come near the undying who never grow old, would — himself a mortal who grows old, here on the earth below, and knowing better — still dwell on the pleasures of beauty and love, and delight in a very long life?

anvaya: अजीर्यताम् अमृतानाम् उपेत्य जीर्यन् क्वधःस्थः प्रजानन् मर्त्यः वर्णरतिप्रमोदान् अभिध्यायन् अतिदीर्घे जीविते कः रमेत ।
syntax: One long rhetorical question. The subject (martyaḥ, picked up by kaḥ) is qualified by participles and an adjective (jīryan, kvadhaḥsthaḥ, prajānan, abhidhyāyan); upetya with its genitive gives the prior action; the main verb is the optative rameta with a locative of the thing delighted in.

ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara divides kvadhaḥsthaḥ as ku (earth) + adhaḥ-stha, ‘dwelling on the earth below’, and records another reading, «क्व तदास्थः», ‘how could he be attached to that?’. Raṅgarāmānuja reads that variant in his text and explains it: «जरामरणशून्यानां मुक्तानां स्वरूपं ज्ञात्वा», knowing the nature of the freed, how would one fix his attachment there? Madhva’s text reads kvādhasthaḥ (corrections.json).

Śaṅkara: the pleasures Death offered, the apsarases and the rest, seen as unstable. Raṅgarāmānuja takes varṇa-rati-pramoda as the delights of the freed in the higher world, which make long earthly life seem short; he glosses the last words as «अत्यल्पे ऐहिके चिरजीविते कः प्रीतिमान् स्यात् इत्यर्थः».

metre.name: triṣṭubh
metre.note: Triṣṭubh. The half-lines count 21 and 22: the second pāda (jīryan martyaḥ kvadhaḥsthaḥ prajānan) has 10 syllables as written, one short of the norm.

beginner: This is Naciketas’ last argument against the offers. He has come face to face with the gods who never grow old and never die. He himself is a mortal, ageing, living down here on the earth, and he knows the difference. Having seen that, he asks, who could still dwell on the pleasures of beauty and love, and be glad of a very long life? The answer the question expects is: no one with understanding. Śaṅkara adds a simple observation about people: everyone wants to rise higher, so once someone has glimpsed what is higher, the lesser offers lose their pull.
analogy: Like someone who has heard a great orchestra live, and no longer wants to spend the evening with a tinny radio, however long it can play.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: A mortal who has approached the unageing immortals, and knows the difference, will not delight in a very long life spent dwelling on beauty, love and pleasure.

commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: As ‘standing on the earth, which is below’: «कुः पृथिवी अधश्चासावन्तरिक्षादिलोकापेक्षया तस्यां तिष्ठतीति क्वधःस्थः». He records another reading, «क्व तदास्थः», ‘how could he be attached to those things?’.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Śaṅkara: everyone wishes to rise higher — «सर्वो ह्युपर्युपर्येव बुभूषति लोकः» — so one who has seen the higher will not be tempted by the lower; reflecting on pleasures as unstable, «अतिदीर्घे जीविते कः विवेकी रमेत».

commentary.label: comparative
commentary.text: Raṅgarāmānuja reads kva tadāsthaḥ, and takes the unageing immortals as the freed: «जरामरणशून्यानां मुक्तानां स्वरूपं ज्ञात्वा». A long life here is very little beside their joy: «अत्यल्पे ऐहिके चिरजीविते कः प्रीतिमान् स्यात् इत्यर्थः».

advaita.text: One who has come near the immortals and knows a higher good will not choose unstable things: «सर्वो ह्युपर्युपर्येव बुभूषति लोकः».

visistadvaita.text: The immortals are the freed selves; knowing their state, one would find even a long earthly life very small: «जरामरणशून्यानां मुक्तानां स्वरूपं ज्ञात्वा».

schools.disagreement: Śaṅkara’s immortals are the gods whom the boy has approached, and the delights are those Death offered; Raṅgarāmānuja’s are the freed, and the delights theirs. They also read the text differently (kvadhaḥsthaḥ / kva tadāsthaḥ). Madhva’s bhāṣya on the passage 1.1.26–29 comments only on ‘the great passing-on’ of 1.1.29.

parallels.note: The Muṇḍaka’s seeker who, having examined the worlds won by works, comes to disenchantment (nirvedam āyāt): the same turning away.

contemporary.text: A longer life is a good, but the verse asks what the length is for. Someone who has glimpsed what does not age measures years differently. This is a reflection, not a claim made by the text.

reflect.beginner: If you could live twice as long, what would you do with the extra years?
reflect.deeper: Does knowing something better change how we value what we already have?
reflect.practice: Recall a moment that felt timeless. Ask what it had that ordinary pleasures lack.

flags.note: kvadhaḥsthaḥ (base); kva tadāsthaḥ, recorded by Śaṅkara and read by Raṅgarāmānuja; kvādhasthaḥ in Madhva’s text (corrections.json).

Raṅgarāmānuja’s gloss of the last pāda begins «अनतिदीर्घे जीविते», as if dividing pramodān anatidīrghe, which the letters of the base do not allow (that would need two n). It may be a gloss rather than a reading; the edition follows atidīrghe.
